rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1, 2.5, 3.3 and Tables 1-3 - the authors flew their own hyperspectral and thermal airborne campaigns on three dates in 2012 over 192 olive plots, ran METRIC at pixel sizes from 5 m to 1 km and report the resulting Rn, G, H, ETc and Kco values; Section 2.3/3.1 - own albedometer measurements compared with Landsat-derived albedo.
rows.notes: The study is a methodological sensitivity analysis of how pixel size affects METRIC energy-balance components and ETc estimates in olive orchards. It estimates crop ET / water requirements from airborne imagery but does not establish or test any irrigation management strategy, nor does it measure water productivity, water savings or any water-conservation outcome. ETc itself is not validated against ground ET measurements (only albedo is validated against field albedometers; the 30 m resolution is used as the reference). At most it supports a precondition of the claim (ability to quantify orchard water requirements with remote sensing), hence upstream.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1, 2.5, 3.3 and Tables 1-3 - own airborne hyperspectral/thermal campaigns (DOY 188, 236, 252 of 2012), METRIC model runs at eleven pixel sizes over 192 olive plots, and own albedometer field measurements (Section 2.3, Fig. 3).
rows.notes: No yield or fruit-quality data are reported anywhere in the study; the only outputs are energy-balance components, instantaneous ETc and crop coefficients at different spatial resolutions. The study therefore provides no evidence of its own that remote-sensing-based water requirement estimates lead to irrigation strategies that optimise olive yield or quality. It supports only the upstream step of estimating ETc/water requirements from airborne imagery, and even that is a resolution-sensitivity comparison rather than a validation against measured ET.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is primary research on the spatial-resolution sensitivity of METRIC energy-balance and ETc estimates in open-canopy olive orchards; it contains no irrigation management trial, water productivity, yield or quality results, so neither claim row is supported beyond the precondition of estimating water requirements.
